cues.en: All right, I'm David Solomon. I'm the president of the Internet Society of New York. And we're presenting Evan Bogan today, who is a professor of law at Columbia, and also the chairman of the Software Freedom Law Center. And he's a tremendous advocate for free software. And we last had him, I guess it was about three years ago.
cues.zh: 好，我是 David Solomon，纽约互联网协会主席。今天我们请到 Evan Bogan，他是哥伦比亚大学法学教授，也是 Software Freedom Law Center 的主席。他是自由软件的坚定倡导者。我们上次请他大概是三年前。

cues.en: Three years ago speaking? A little ways back. And I remember, OK, that he said at that time, well, basically we've won. And it was true in the sense that free open source software is and was used now on every environment from a handheld computer or a smartphone to... Oh, OK. All right. OK. Is now used on every type of computer imaginable from a... OK. It's for the webcast. Oh, OK.
cues.zh: 三年前来讲过？有一阵子了。我记得，好，他当时说，基本上我们已经赢了。这确实如此，因为自由开源软件现在和过去都用在了各种环境里，从手持电脑或智能手机到……哦，好。行。好。现在用在了你能想到的每一种计算机上，从……好。这是给网络直播的。哦，好。

cues.en: All right, one more time. OK, it's used on every type of device from a smartphone to a supercomputer. But happily, we are faced with new challenges in terms of software freedom, the freedom to know what the software you use actually does, how it works, to modify it and customize it and enhance it, and to freely redistribute it. These freedoms are challenged by the new
cues.zh: 好，再来一次。好，它被用于从智能手机到超级计算机的各种设备。但幸运的是，我们在软件自由方面面临新的挑战：有权知道你所使用的软件到底做什么、如何运作，有权修改、定制和改进它，并自由再分发它。这些自由正受到新的

cues.en: cloud computing services and web 2.0 services where basically you don't even know where physically your data or your
cues.zh: 云计算服务和 Web 2.0 服务的挑战——基本上你甚至不知道自己的数据或你的

cues.en: application or process resides. It could be anywhere in any country with different laws and different kinds of law enforcement. And again, there is the issue of who actually owns your data when, for example, you're using a service like Gmail where your data resides on their Google servers. And you really don't know what they're doing with it, although they promise that they're going to be not evil. So on that note, I'd like to throw this over to Evan.
cues.zh: 应用或进程实际位于哪里。它可能在任何一个国家，有着不同的法律和不同类型的执法方式。再者，还有一个问题：当你使用像 Gmail 这样的服务时，你的数据到底归谁所有——你的数据存放在他们的 Google 服务器上。而你其实并不知道他们拿它做什么，尽管他们承诺会“不作恶”。那么说到这里，我想把话题交给 Evan。

cues.en: Thank you. Thank you, David. It's a pleasure to be here. I would love to think that the reason that we're all here on a Friday night is because my speeches are so good. I actually have no idea why we're all here on a Friday night, but I'm very grateful for the invitation. I am the person who had no date tonight, and so it was particularly convenient that I was invited for now.
cues.zh: 谢谢。谢谢你，David。很高兴来到这里。我很愿意相信，我们周五晚上都聚在这里，是因为我的演讲太精彩了。其实我完全不知道我们周五晚上为什么都在这儿，但我非常感激这次邀请。我就是今晚没约会对象的那个人，所以现在能被邀请来，特别方便。

cues.en: Of course, I didn't have any date tonight. Everybody knows that. My calendar's on the web, right? The problem is that problem, right? It is that problem. Our calendar's on the web. Our location's on the web. You have a cell phone and you have a cell phone network provider. And if your cell phone network provider is sprint,
cues.zh: 当然，我今晚没有约会对象。大家都知道。我的日历在网上，对吧？问题就是那个问题，对吧？就是那个问题。我们的日历在网上。我们的位置在网上。你有手机，也有手机网络运营商。如果你的手机网络运营商是 Sprint，

cues.en: Then we can tell you that several million times last year somebody who has a law enforcement ID card in his pocket somewhere went to the Sprint website and asked for the real-time location of somebody with a telephone number and was given it. Several million times. Just like that. We know that because Sprint admits that they have a website where anybody with a law enforcement ID can go and find the real-time location of anybody with a Sprint cell phone.
cues.zh: 那么我们可以告诉你，去年有几百万次，某个口袋里装着执法部门证件的人，去了 Sprint 网站，要求获取某个电话号码对应人员的实时位置，然后就拿到了。几百万次。就这么简单。我们知道这件事，因为 Sprint 承认，他们有一个网站，任何持有执法部门证件的人都能上去，查到任何使用 Sprint 手机的人的实时位置。

cues.en: And we don't know that about AT&T and Verizon because they haven't told us. But that's the only reason we don't know, right? Because they haven't told us. That's a service that you think of as traditional service telephony. But the deal that you get with the traditional service called telephony now includes a thing you didn't know, like spying. It's not a service to you, but it's a service.
cues.zh: 我们不知道 AT&T 和 Verizon 的这种情况，因为他们没告诉我们。但这就是我们不知道的唯一原因，对吧？因为他们没告诉我们。那是你以为的传统服务——电话服务。但你现在从所谓电话服务这项传统服务里得到的交易，已经包含了你不知道的东西，比如监视。这对你来说不是服务，但它是一项服务。

cues.en: And you get it for free with your service contract for telephony. You get for free the service of advertising with your Gmail, which means, of course, there's another service behind, which is untouched by human hands semantic analysis of your email. I still don't understand why anybody wants that. I still don't understand why anybody uses it, but people do.
cues.zh: 而且你用电话服务合同免费得到了它。你用 Gmail 免费得到了广告服务，当然，这意味着背后还有另一项服务：对你的邮件进行不经过人手的语义分析。我还是不明白为什么有人想要这个。我还是不明白为什么有人用它，但人们确实在用。

cues.en: including the very sophisticated and thoughtful people in this room. And you get free email service and some storage which is worth exactly a penny and a half at the current price of storage. And you get spying all the time. And for free. Two. And your calendars on the web and everybody can see whether you have a date Friday night and you have a status. Single looking. And you get a service for free. Advertising single looking and spying.
cues.zh: 包括在座这些非常老练、很有想法的人。你还能得到免费邮件服务和一些存储空间，按现在的存储价格，正好值一便士半。你还一直享受被监视，而且免费。第二点。你的日历放在网上，所有人都能看到你周五晚上有没有约会，还有你的状态：单身，寻觅中。你免费得到一项服务：广告、单身寻觅和监视。

cues.en: with it, for free. And it all sort of just grewed up that way, right? In the blink of an eye, and here we are. And what's that got to do with open source? Well, in fact, it doesn't have anything to do with open source, but it has a whole lot to do with free software. Yet another reason why Stallman was right. It's the freedom, right? So we need to back up a little bit and figure out where we actually are.
cues.zh: 有了它，还免费。而这一切差不多就是这么长起来的，对吧？一眨眼，我们就到这儿了。那这跟开源有什么关系？其实，它跟开源没什么关系，但跟自由软件关系很大。这又是 Stallman 说对了的一个理由。关键是自由，对吧？所以我们得稍微退一步，搞清楚自己到底处在什么位置。

cues.en: and how we actually got here, and probably even more important, whether we can get out, and if so, how. And it isn't a pretty story. At all. David's right. I mean, I can hardly begin by saying that we won, given that spying comes free with everything now. But we haven't lost. We've just really bamboozled ourselves. And we're gonna have to unbamboozle ourselves real quickly, or we're gonna bamboozle a lot of other innocent people who...
cues.zh: 以及我们究竟是怎么走到这一步的，还有可能更重要的是，我们能不能走出去，如果能，又该怎么走。这可不是个美好的故事。一点也不。David 说得对。我是说，既然如今监控已经随一切免费附赠，我实在很难开口说我们赢了。但我们也没输。我们只是把自己彻底忽悠了。而我们得赶紧把自己从这种忽悠里弄醒，否则我们还会去忽悠很多无辜的人，他们……

cues.en: didn't know that we were throwing away their privacy for them forever. It begins, of course, with the Internet, which is why it's really nice to be here talking to the Internet Society, a society dedicated to the health expansion and theoretical elaboration of a peer-to-peer network called The Internet.
cues.zh: 不知道我们正在替他们永远丢掉隐私。当然，这一切始于互联网，所以很高兴来到这里与互联网协会交流——这个协会致力于一个名为互联网的点对点网络的健康发展与理论阐述。

cues.en: designed as a network of peers without any intrinsic need for hierarchical or structural control and assuming that every switch in the net is an independent freestanding entity whose volition is equivalent to the volition of the human beings who own and control it. That's the design of the net which whether you're thinking about it as glued together with IPv4 or that
cues.zh: 它被设计成对等网络，本质上不需要层级或结构性控制，并假定网络中的每个交换机都是独立自主的实体，其意志等同于拥有和控制它的人的意志。这就是网络的设计——无论你把它看作由 IPv4 粘合起来，还是那个

cues.en: wonderful improvement, IPv6 we will never use, apparently. It still assumes peer communications. Of course, it never really, really, really worked out that way. There was nothing in the technical design to prevent it, not at any rate in the technical design of the interconnection of nodes and their communication. There was a software problem.
cues.zh: 了不起的改进——IPv6，显然我们永远不会用。它仍然假定对等通信。当然，现实从来、从来、从来都不是那样。技术设计里没有任何东西阻止它，至少节点互联及其通信的技术设计中没有。问题出在软件上。

cues.en: It's a simple software problem, and it has a simple two-syllable name. Its name is Microsoft. Conceptually, conceptually, there was a network which was designed as a system of peer nodes, but the operating software which occupied the network in an increasingly, I'll use the word, they use it about us, why can't I use it back viral way over the course of a decade and a half?
cues.zh: 这是个简单的软件问题，它有一个简单的、两个音节的名字。它的名字是 Microsoft。从概念上说，从概念上说，曾经有一个网络，被设计成由对等节点组成的系统，但占据这个网络的运行软件，在十五年左右的时间里，以一种越来越——我就用这个词，他们拿它来说我们，我为什么不能反过来用——病毒式的方式扩张？

cues.en: The software that came to occupy the network was built around a very clear idea that had nothing to do with peers. It was called server-client architecture. And the idea that the network was a network of peers was hard to perceive after a while, particularly if you were, let us say, ordinary human being, that is not a computer engineer, scientist or researcher, not a hacker, not a geek.
cues.zh: 最终占据这个网络的软件，围绕一个与对等节点毫无关系的清晰理念构建。它叫客户端-服务器架构。而过了一阵子，网络是由对等节点组成的网络这一观念就很难被感知，尤其如果你——这么说吧——是普通人，不是计算机工程师、科学家或研究者，不是黑客，不是极客。

cues.en: If you were an ordinary human being, it was hard to perceive that the underlying architecture of the net was meant to be about peerage because the operating system software with which you interacted very strongly instantiated the idea of the server and client architecture. In fact, of course, if you think about it, it was even worse than that. The thing called Windows was a degenerate version of a thing called X-Windows.
cues.zh: 如果你是个普通人，很难察觉到网络的底层架构本意是关于对等关系的，因为你交互所用的操作系统软件非常强烈地实例化了服务器-客户端架构这一理念。实际上，仔细想想，情况还更糟。那个叫 Windows 的东西，是叫 X-Windows 的东西的退化版本。

cues.en: It, too, thought about the world in a server-client architecture, but what we would now think of as backwards. The server was the thing at the human being's end, remember? That was the basic X-Windows conception of the world. It served communications with human beings at the endpoints of the net to processes located at arbitrary places near the center, in the middle, or at the edge of the net.
cues.zh: 它也以服务器-客户端架构来理解世界，只不过以我们今天的眼光看，方向是反的。还记得吗？服务器是位于人这一端的东西。这就是 X-Windows 对世界的基本构想。它负责打通通信：一端是网络端点处的人类，另一端是分布在任意位置的进程——靠近中心、在中间，或在网络边缘。

cues.en: It was the great idea of Windows in an odd way to create a political archetype in the net which reduced the human being to the client and produced a big centralized computer which we might have called a server which now provided things to the human being on take it or leave it terms. They were of course quite take it or leave it terms.
cues.zh: 说来奇怪，Windows 的一大创举，就是在网络中造出一种政治原型：它把人贬为客户端，并造出一台大型集中式计算机——我们或许可以称之为服务器——由它以“要么接受、要么拉倒”的条件向人提供东西。当然，那些条件确实相当“要么接受、要么拉倒”。

cues.en: and unfortunately everybody took it because they didn't know how to leave once they got in. Now the net was made of servers in the center and clients at the edge. Clients had rather little power and servers had quite a lot. As storage gets cheaper, as processing gets cheaper, and as complex services that scale in ways that are hard to use small computers for or at any rate
cues.zh: 不幸的是，所有人都接受了它，因为一旦进去就不知道该怎么离开。现在这个网络由中心的服务器和边缘的客户端组成。客户端能力相当弱，服务器则强得多。随着存储越来越便宜、处理能力越来越便宜，以及复杂服务以小型计算机难以胜任的方式扩展，或者至少说

cues.en: these aggregated collections of small computers for, the most important of which is search. As services began to populate that net, the hierarchical nature of the net came to seem like it was meant to be there. The net was made of servers and clients, and the clients were the guys at the edge representing human beings, and servers were things in the middle with lots of power and lots of data. Now, one more thing happened about that time.
cues.zh: 这些小型计算机的聚合集合所能处理的服务，其中最重要的就是搜索。随着服务开始填充这个网络，网络的分层特性开始显得像是本来就该如此。网络由服务器和客户端组成：客户端是处在边缘、代表人类的那群人，服务器则是位于中间、拥有强大算力和海量数据的东西。大约就在那时，又发生了一件事。

cues.en: It didn't happen in Microsoft Windows computers, although it happened in Microsoft Windows servers. And it happened more in sensible operating systems like Unix and GNU-Linux and other ones. Namely, servers kept logs. That's a good thing to do. Computers ought to keep logs. It's a very wise decision when making a computer operating software to keep logs. It helps with debugging, makes efficiencies attainable.
cues.zh: 这没有发生在 Microsoft Windows 计算机上，尽管它发生在 Microsoft Windows 服务器上。而在 Unix、GNU-Linux 以及其他更合理的操作系统上，这种情况更多。也就是说，服务器会保留日志。这是件好事。计算机就应该保留日志。开发计算机操作系统软件时，保留日志是非常明智的决定。它有助于调试，也能让效率提升成为可能。

cues.en: makes it possible to study the actual operations of computers in the real world. It's a very good idea. But if you have a system which centralizes servers, and the servers centralize their logs, then you are creating vast repositories of hierarchically organized data about people at the edges of the network that they do not control. And unless they are experienced in the operation of servers, will not understand
cues.zh: 它使研究现实世界中计算机的实际运行成为可能。这想法很好。但如果你有一个集中管理服务器的系统，而服务器又集中管理它们的日志，那你就在制造庞大的、按层级组织的数据仓库，记录的是网络边缘那些人的数据，而这些人并不控制这些数据。除非他们熟悉服务器运维，否则不会理解

cues.en: the comprehensiveness of, will not understand the meaningfulness of, will not understand the aggregatability of. So we built a network out of a communications architecture designed for peering, which we defined in client-server style, which we then defined to be the disempowered client at the edge and the server in the middle.
cues.zh: 这些数据的全面性，不会理解其意义，也不会理解其可聚合性。于是我们用一套为对等互联设计的通信架构来构建网络，却以客户端-服务器风格来定义它，随后又把它定义为边缘处被削权的客户端和位于中间的服务器。

cues.en: We aggregated processing and storage increasingly in the middle and we kept the logs That is information about the flows of information in the net in centralized places far from the human beings who controlled or at any rate thought they controlled the operation of the computers that increasingly Dominated their lives. This was a recipe for disaster This was a recipe
cues.zh: 我们越来越多地把处理和存储集中到中间，并把日志——也就是网络中信息流动的信息——保存在集中化场所，远离那些控制着、或者至少自认为控制着越来越主导他们生活的计算机运行的人类。这是灾难的配方，这是

cues.en: for disaster. Now, I haven't mentioned yet the word cloud, which I was dealt on the top of the deck when I received the news that I was talking here tonight about privacy in the cloud. I haven't mentioned the word cloud because the word cloud doesn't really mean anything very much. In other words, the disaster we are having is not the catastrophe of the cloud.
cues.zh: 灾难的配方。现在，我还没提到“云”这个词；当我得知今晚要在这里谈云中的隐私时，这就像发到我手里最上面的那张牌。我一直没提“云”这个词，因为“云”这个词其实没多大意义。换句话说，我们正遭遇的灾难并不是云带来的灾难。

cues.en: The disaster we are having is the catastrophe of the way we misunderstood the net under the assistance of the unfree software that helped us to understand it. What cloud means is that servers have ceased to be made of iron. Cloud means virtualization of servers has occurred. So, out here in the dusty edges of the galaxy where we live in disempowered clienthood,
cues.zh: 我们正在遭遇的灾难，是在那些帮助我们理解网络的非自由软件协助下，我们误解网络所造成的大灾难。云意味着服务器不再由铁构成。云意味着服务器已经虚拟化。所以，在我们身处无权客户端地位的、星系尘埃边缘的这里，

cues.en: Nothing very much has changed. As you walk inward towards the center of the galaxy, it gets more fuzzy than it used to. We resolve now halo, where we used to see actual stars, you know, servers with switches and buttons you can push and such. Instead, what has happened, of course, is that iron no longer represents a single server. Iron is merely a place where servers could be.
cues.zh: 并没有太大变化。当你向内走向星系中心，它会变得比过去更模糊。我们现在分辨出的是光晕，而过去我们看到的是真正的星星，你知道，就是带开关和按钮、能按的服务器之类。当然，实际发生的是，铁不再代表单台服务器。铁只是服务器可能存在的地方。

cues.en: And so cloud means servers have gained freedom. Freedom to move, freedom to dance, freedom to combine and separate and re-aggregate and do all kinds of tricks. Servers have gained freedom, clients have gained nothing. Welcome to the cloud. It's a minor modification of the recipe for disaster. It improves the operability of systems that control
cues.zh: 所以，云意味着服务器获得了自由。移动的自由，舞动的自由，组合、分离、再聚合、玩各种花样的自由。服务器获得了自由，客户端却一无所获。欢迎来到云。这不过是灾难配方的一处小改动。它提升了控制……

cues.en: the clients out there who were meant to be peers in a net made of equal things. So that's the architecture of the catastrophe. If you think about it, each step in that architectural evolution away from a network made of peers to servers that serve the communication with human beings to clients which are programs running on heavy iron.
cues.zh: 外部那些客户端的系统的可运维性——这些客户端本应是平等节点构成的网络中的对等方。所以，这就是灾难的架构。想想看，这种架构演进中的每一步，都是从对等节点构成的网络，走向为与人类通信服务的服务器，再走向客户端——也就是运行在重型机器上的程序。

cues.en: to clients which are the computers that people actually use in a fairly disempowered state and servers are high concentration of powers in the net, to servers are virtual processes running in clouds of iron at the center of an increasingly hot galaxy and the clients are out there in the dusty spiral arms. All of those decisions architecturally were made without any discussion of the social consequences long-term.
cues.zh: 客户端是人们实际使用、处于相当弱势状态的计算机，而服务器是网络中高度集中的权力；服务器是在日益炽热的星系中心、铁云中运行的虚拟进程，客户端则在外侧布满尘埃的旋臂上。所有这些架构决策在做出时，都没有讨论过长期的社会后果。

cues.en: part of our general difficulty in talking about the social consequences of technology during the great period of invention of the internet done by computer scientists who weren't terribly interested in sociology, social psychology, or, with a few shining exceptions, freedom. So we got an architecture which was very subject to misuse. Indeed, it was, in a way, begging to be misused.
cues.zh: 我们在讨论技术的社会后果时普遍感到困难，部分原因在于：互联网的伟大发明时期是由计算机科学家主导的，而他们并不太关心社会学、社会心理学，或者——除了少数闪光的例外——自由。于是我们得到了一种极易被滥用的架构。事实上，从某种意义上说，它简直是在招引滥用。

cues.en: And now we are getting the misuse that we set up. Because we have thinned the clients out further and further and further. In fact, we made them mobile. We put them in our pockets and we started strolling around with them. There are a lot of reasons for making clients disempowered. And there are even more reasons for disempowering the people who own the clients and who might
cues.zh: 现在，我们正在收获自己造成的滥用。因为我们把客户端越做越瘦，越做越瘦，越做越瘦。事实上，我们让它们移动起来。我们把它们放进口袋，开始带着它们四处走动。让客户端失去权力有很多理由。而让拥有这些客户端、并且可能……的人失去权力，理由甚至更多。

cues.en: quaintly be thought of as the people who ought to control it. If you think for just a moment how many people have an interest in disempowering the clients that are the mobile telephones, you will see what I mean. There are many overlapping rights owners as they think of themselves, each of whom has a stake in disempowering a client at the edge of a network to prevent particular hardware from being moved from one network to another.
cues.zh: 不妨古怪地把这些人看作理应控制它的人。只要稍想一下，有多少人有动机去削弱作为客户端的手机，你就会明白我的意思。有许多自认为是权利所有者的人，他们的权利相互重叠；每个人都希望削弱网络边缘的客户端，以阻止特定硬件从一个网络转移到另一个网络。

cues.en: to prevent particular hardware from playing music, not bought at the great monopoly of music in the sky, to disable competing video delivery services in favor of new chips I founded myself that won't run popular video standards, good or bad. There were a lot of business models.
cues.zh: 阻止特定硬件播放并非从云端音乐大垄断者那里买来的音乐；为了扶持我自己创办的新芯片，禁用与之竞争的视频分发服务，而这些芯片不会运行流行的视频标准，无论好坏。当时有很多商业模式。

cues.en: that are based around mucking with the control over client hardware and software at the edge to deprive the human being who has quaintly thought that she purchased it from actually occupying the position that capitalism says owners are always in, that is, of total control. In fact, what we have, as I said a couple of years ago, in between the appearances here at another NYU function, in fact, what we have are things we call platforms.
cues.zh: 这些商业模式的核心，是在边缘端操控对客户端硬件和软件的控制权，使那些天真地以为自己买下了它的人，无法真正占据资本主义所说的所有者始终所处的位置——也就是完全控制权。事实上，正如我几年前在纽约大学另一场活动上露面时说过的那样，事实上，我们拥有的是我们称之为平台的东西。

cues.en: The word platform, like the word cloud, doesn't inherently mean anything. It's thrown around a lot in business talk. But basically what platform means is places you can't leave, stuff you're stuck to, things that don't let you off. That's platforms. And the net, once it became a hierarchically architected zone with servers in the center and increasingly disempowered clients at the edge, becomes
cues.zh: 平台这个词，跟云这个词一样，本身并没有什么含义。商业话术里到处都在用它。但基本上，平台的意思就是那些你离不开的地方、你被绑住的东西、不让你脱身的东西。这就是平台。而互联网一旦变成一个层级化架构的区域——服务器在中心，边缘的客户端越来越没有权力——它就变成了

cues.en: the zone of platforms. And platform making becomes the order of the day. Some years ago, a very shrewd lawyer who works in the industry said to me, Microsoft was never really a software company. Microsoft was a platform management company. And I thought, yes, shot through the heart. So we had a lot of platform managers in a hierarchically organized network.
cues.zh: 平台的领地。而打造平台就成了头等大事。几年前，业内一位非常精明的律师对我说，微软从来就不是一家真正的软件公司。微软是一家平台管理公司。我心想，对，一箭穿心。所以，在一个层级化组织的网络里，我们有一大堆平台管理者。

cues.en: And we began to evolve services. Services is a complicated word. It's not meaningless by any means, but it's very tricky to describe it. We use it for a lot of different things. We badly need an analytical taxonomy of services, as my friend and colleague Philippe Begrin in Paris pointed out some two years or three ago. Taxonomies of services involve questions of simplicity,
cues.zh: 我们开始演进服务。服务这个词很复杂。它绝非没有意义，但非常难描述。我们把它用在许多不同的事情上。我们非常需要一套对服务的分析性分类法，就像我巴黎的朋友兼同事 Philippe Begrin 大约两三年前指出的那样。服务的分类法涉及简单性、

cues.en: complexity, scale, and control. To take an example, we might define a dichotomy between complex and simple services, in which simple services are things that any computer can perform for any other computer if it wants to, and complex services are things you can't do with a computer. You must do with clusters or structures of some computational or administrative complexity. Search
cues.zh: 复杂性、规模和可控性等问题。举个例子，我们可以在复杂服务和简单服务之间做一个二分：简单服务是任何计算机只要愿意就能为任何其他计算机执行的事情，而复杂服务则是单台计算机做不了的事情。你必须借助具有某种计算或管理复杂性的集群或结构来完成。搜索

cues.en: is a complex service. Indeed, search is the archetypal complex service. Given the one-way nature of links in the web and other elements of the data architecture that we are now also living with, that's another talk, another time, search is not a thing that we can easily distribute. The power in the market of our friends at Google depends entirely on the fact that search is not easily distributed.
cues.zh: 搜索是一项复杂服务。实际上，搜索就是复杂服务的典型。鉴于网络链接的单向性，以及我们如今也身处其中的数据架构的其他要素——那是另一场演讲、另一个话题了——搜索并不是我们能轻易做分布式部署的东西。我们在 Google 的朋友们之所以拥有市场力量，完全取决于搜索不容易被分布式化。

cues.en: It is a complex service that must be centrally organized and centrally delivered. It must crawl the web in a unilateral direction, link by link, figuring out where everything is in order to help you find it when you need it. And in order to do that, at least so far, we have not evolved good algorithmic and delivery structures for doing it in a decentralized way. So search.
cues.zh: 它是一项必须集中组织、集中交付的复杂服务。它必须沿着单向方向、一个链接接一个链接地抓取网络，弄清所有内容的位置，以便在你需要时帮你找到它。而要做到这一点，至少到目前为止，我们还没有发展出良好的算法与交付结构，来以去中心化的方式实现它。所以，搜索就是这样。

cues.en: becomes a archetypal complex service and it draws onto itself a business model for its monetization. Advertising in the 20th century was a random activity. You threw things out and hoped they worked. Advertising in the 21st century is an exquisitely precise activity. You wait for a guy to want something and then you send him advertisements about what he wants and bingo, it works like magic.
cues.zh: 它成了一种典型的复杂服务，并将一套变现商业模式吸附到自身。20世纪的广告是一种随机行为。你把东西撒出去，然后指望它奏效。21世纪的广告则是一种极其精准的行为。你等一个人产生某种需求，然后把他想要之物的广告发给他，砰，像魔法一样奏效。

cues.en: So, of course, on the underside of a complex service called search, there is a theoretically simple service called advertising, which, when unified to a complex service, increases its efficiency by orders of magnitude. And the increase of the efficiency of the simple service, when combined with the complex one, produces an enormous surplus revenue flow, which can be used to strengthen search even more. But that's the innocent.
cues.zh: 所以，当然，在搜索这项复杂服务的底层，有一项理论上很简单的服务，叫广告；当它与复杂服务结合时，会把效率提升数个数量级。而这项简单服务的效率提升，与复杂服务结合后，会产生巨额超额收入流，又能用来进一步增强搜索。但这还只是无害的部分。

cues.en: part of the story. And we don't remain in the innocent part of the story for a variety of reasons. I won't be tedious in Marx's essay on a Friday night and say because the bourgeoisie is constantly engaged in destructively reinventing and improving its own activities. And I won't be moralistic on a Friday night that you can't do that and say because sin is ineradicable and human beings are fallen creatures.
cues.zh: 这是故事的一部分。由于种种原因，我们不会停留在故事中天真的部分。周五晚上，我不想在 Marx 的文章里絮叨地说，因为资产阶级一直在破坏性地重塑和改进自身活动。周五晚上，我也不想道德说教地说你不能那么做，因为罪恶无法根除、人类是堕落的生物。

cues.en: Greed is one of the sins we cannot avoid committing. I will just say that as a sort of ordinary social process, we don't stop at innocent. We go on, which surely is the thing you should say on a Friday night. And so we went on. Now, where we went on is really towards the discovery that all of this would be even better if you had all the logs of everything. Because once you have all the logs of everything, then...
cues.zh:
贪婪是我们无法避免犯下的罪之一。
我只想说，作为一种普通的社会过程，我们不会止步于无辜。
我们会继续，这当然是周五晚上该说的话。
于是我们就继续了。
现在，我们继续的方向，其实是去发现：如果你拥有所有事物的全部日志，这一切会更好。
因为一旦你有了所有事物的全部日志，那么……

cues.en: Every simple service is suddenly a gold mine waiting to happen. And we blew it because the architecture of the net put the logs in the wrong place. They put the logs where innocence would be tempted. They put the logs where the fallen state of human beings implies eventually bad trouble. And we got it. The cloud means that we can't even point in the direction of the server anymore.
cues.zh: 每个简单的服务突然都成了一座等着被挖的金矿。而我们把它搞砸了，因为网络架构把日志放错了地方。他们把日志放在会诱使无辜者犯错的位置。他们把日志放在人性堕落状态下最终注定会引发大麻烦的位置。而我们果然中招了。云计算意味着，我们甚至再也无法指出服务器所在的方向。

cues.en: And because we can't even point in the direction of the server anymore, we don't have extra technical or non-technical means of reliable control over this disaster in slow motion. You can make a rule about logs or data flow or preservation or control or access or disclosure.
cues.zh: 而且，因为我们甚至再也无法指出服务器所在的方向，我们就没有额外的技术或非技术手段来可靠控制这场慢动作灾难。你可以针对日志、数据流、保存、控制、访问或披露制定规则。

cues.en: But your laws are human laws and they occupy particular territory and the server is in the cloud and that means the server is always One step ahead of any rule you make or two or three or six or poof I just realized I'm subject to regulation. I think I'll move to Oceana now
cues.zh: 但你们的法律是人类的法，只管辖特定领土，而服务器在云端，这意味着服务器总比你制定的任何规则快一步——或者快两步、三步、六步——或者噗，我刚意识到自己受监管了。我想我现在要搬去 Oceana 了。

cues.en: Which means that in effect we lost the ability to use either legal regulation or anything about the physical architecture of the network to interfere with the process of falling away from innocence that was now inevitable in the stage I'm talking about, what we might call late Google stage one. It is here of course that Mr. Zuckerberg enters.
cues.zh: 这意味着，实际上我们已经失去了用法律监管、或用网络物理架构中的任何东西来干预“脱离纯真”过程的能力；在我所说的这个阶段，这已是不可避免，也就是我们或许可称为“Google 晚期第一阶段”的阶段。当然，正是在这里，Zuckerberg 先生登场了。

cues.en: The human race has, you know, a susceptibility to harm. But Mr. Zuckerberg has attained an unenviable record. He has done more harm to the human race than anybody else his age. Right? Because he harnessed, you know, Friday night, that is, everybody needs to get laid.
cues.zh: 人类嘛，你知道，本来就容易受到伤害。但扎克伯格先生创下了一个不值得羡慕的纪录。他对人类造成的伤害，比同龄任何人都多。对吧？因为他利用了，你知道，周五夜晚——也就是人人都想上床这件事。

cues.en: And he turned it into a structure for degenerating the integrity of human personality. And he has, to a remarkable extent, succeeded with a very poor deal. Namely, I will give you free web hosting and some PHP doodads. And you get spying for free all the time. And it works.
cues.zh: 他把它变成了一种腐蚀人格完整性的结构。而且他靠一个非常糟糕的交易，取得了惊人的成功。也就是：我给你免费网站托管和一些 PHP 小玩意儿。而我则一直免费监视你。而且这还真管用。

cues.en: But that's the sad part. It works. How could that have happened? There was no architectural reason, really, right? There was no architectural reason, really. Facebook is the web with I keep all the logs. How do you feel about that? It's a terrarium for what it feels like to live in a panopticon build out of web parts.
cues.zh: 但可悲的地方在于：它居然有效。这怎么会发生？真的没有什么架构上的理由，对吧？真的没有架构上的理由。Facebook 就是互联网，而我把所有日志都留着。你对此怎么看？它是个生态缸，让你体会住在由网络部件搭成的全景监控监狱里是什么感觉。

cues.en: It shouldn't be allowed. It comes to that. It shouldn't be allowed. That's a very poor way to deliver those services. They are grossly overpriced at spying all the time. They are not technically innovative. They depend upon an architecture subject to misuse. And the business model that supports them is misuse. There isn't any other business model for them. This is bad.
cues.zh: 这不该被允许。事情就走到这一步。这不该被允许。用这种方式提供那些服务太糟糕了。它们一直监视，收费却高得离谱。技术上毫无创新。它们依赖一种容易被滥用的架构。而支撑它们的商业模式就是滥用。它们没有别的商业模式。这很糟。

cues.en: It's bad. I'm not suggesting it should be illegal. It should be obsolete. We're technologists. We should fix it. Well, I'm glad I'm with you so far. When I come to how we should fix it a little later, I hope you'll still be with me. Because then we can get it done. But let's say for now that that's a really good example.
cues.zh: 这很糟糕。我不是说它应该违法。它应该被淘汰。我们是技术人。我们应该解决它。还好，到目前为止你们还认同我。等我稍后讲到该怎么解决时，希望你们还能认同我。因为那样我们才能真正把它搞定。不过现在先这么说：这是个非常好的例子。

cues.en: of where we went wrong and what happened to us because it's trickier with Gmail because of that magical untouched by human handsiness. When I say to my students, why do you let people read your email? They say, but nobody's reading my email.
cues.zh: 说明我们哪里做错了、我们遭遇了什么，因为放到 Gmail 上就更棘手了，因为那种神奇“没人碰过”的感觉。当我问学生，你们为什么让别人读你们的邮件？他们说，可没人在读我的邮件啊。

cues.en: There's no human being ever touch of it that would freak me out. I would be creeped out You know if guys at Google were reading my email But that's not happening, so I don't have a problem Now this they cannot say about Facebook indeed They know way too much about Facebook if they let themselves really know it you have read the stuff and you know Facebook workers know who's about to have a love affair before the people do
cues.zh: 从来没有真人去碰它，这一点不会让我发毛。要是 Google 的人真的在读我的邮件，我会毛骨悚然——但这事没发生，所以我不觉得有问题。可这一点，Facebook 就不能这么说了，真的。要是他们真去了解，Facebook 知道得实在太多了。你读过那些东西就知道，Facebook 员工比当事人还先知道谁要谈恋爱。

cues.en: because they can see X obsessively checking the Facebook page of Y. There's some very nice research done a couple of years ago at MIT in a seminar I shouldn't name by students I'm not going to describe because they were a little denting to the Facebook terms of service in the course of their research. They were just scraping. But the purpose of their scraping was to demonstrate that you could find closeted homosexuals on Facebook.
cues.zh: 因为他们能看到 X 疯狂刷 Y 的 Facebook 页面。几年前 MIT 有个很不错的研究，是在一个我不该点名的研讨班上做的，做研究的学生我也不想描述，因为他们在研究过程中有点触犯 Facebook 的服务条款。他们只是抓取数据。但他们抓取数据的目的是证明，你可以在 Facebook 上找到未出柜的同性恋者。

cues.en: They don't say anything about their sexual orientation group their friends Their friends are out Their interests are the interests of their friends who are out Their photographs are tagged with their friends who are out and they're out except they're not out They're just out in Facebook if anybody knows
cues.zh: 他们从不说自己的性取向。看看他们的朋友：朋友出柜了；他们的兴趣就是那些出柜朋友的兴趣；他们的照片被出柜的朋友打了标签；于是他们也算出柜了——只不过他们并没有出柜。他们只是在 Facebook 上出柜了，如果有人知道的话。

cues.en: which is not what they had in mind, surely, and not what we have in mind for them, surely. In fact, the degree of potential informational inequality and disruption and difficulty that arises from a misunderstanding, a heuristic error in the minds of human beings about what is and is not discoverable about them is now our biggest privacy problem.
cues.zh: 这肯定不是他们本意，也肯定不是我们为他们设想的。事实上，人类头脑中对“关于他们什么能被发现、什么不能被发现的”存在误解——一种启发式错误——由此产生的潜在信息不平等、干扰和困难程度，如今已是我们最大的隐私问题。

cues.en: My students, and I suspect many of the students of the teachers in this room too, show constantly in our dialogue the difficulty. They still think of privacy as the one secret I don't want revealed. And that's not the problem. Their problem is all the stuff that's the cruft, the data dandruff of life, that they don't think of a secret in any way but which aggregates to stuff that they don't want anybody to know.
cues.zh: 我的学生，而且我猜这个房间里许多老师的学生也一样，在我们的对话中不断表现出这种困难。他们仍然把隐私想成那一个我不想被揭露的秘密。但问题不在这里。他们的问题是所有那些杂物，生活中掉落的“数据皮屑”，他们根本不觉得那算秘密，但这些信息聚合起来，就成了他们不想让任何人知道的东西。

cues.en: which aggregates in fact not just the stuff they don't want people to know, but to predictive models about them that they would be very creeped out to think could exist at all. The simplicity with which you can unanonymize, theoretically anonymize data. The ease with which from multiple sources available to you through third and fourth party commercial transactions for information, you can assemble data maps of people's lives.
cues.zh:
它聚合的不仅是他们不愿让人知道的信息，还会形成关于他们的预测模型——一想到这种模型可能存在，他们就会毛骨悚然。
把理论上已匿名的数据去匿名化，竟如此简单。
通过第三方、第四方信息商业交易获得的多个来源，你能轻松拼出人们生活的数据地图。

cues.en: The ease with which once you begin constraining by the few things you know about people, the data available to you, you can quickly infer immense amounts more. My friend and colleague Bradley Kuhn, who works at the Software Freedom Law Center, is one of those archaic human beings who believes that a social security number is a private thing. And he goes to great lengths to make sure that his social security number is not disclosed.
cues.zh: 令人惊讶的是，一旦你开始用关于人们的少量已知信息和你手头可用的数据来约束，就能很快推断出海量多得多的信息。我的朋友兼同事 Bradley Kuhn 在 Software Freedom Law Center 工作，他属于那种老派的人，认为社会安全号码是私密信息。而且他想方设法确保自己的社会安全号码不被泄露。

cues.en: which is his right, or our law, oddly enough. Though, try and get health insurance, or get a safe deposit box, or in fact operate the business at all. We bend over backwards sometimes in the operation of our business because, Bradley's Social Security number is a secret. And I said to him one day, you know, it's over now because Google knows your Social Security number.
cues.zh: 这按理说是他的权利，或者说是我们的法律，说来也怪。可你试试去办医疗保险、租个银行保险箱，或者干脆正常经营业务看看。我们经营业务时有时得费尽周折，就因为 Bradley 的社会安全号码是个秘密。有一天我对他说，你知道吗，现在没用了，因为 Google 知道你的社会安全号码。

cues.en: He said, no, they don't. I've never told anybody. I said, yeah. But they know the Social Security number of everybody else born in Baltimore. Yours is the other one. And as you know, I mean, that's true, right? The data that we infer is the data in the holes between the data we already know if we know enough things.
cues.zh: 他说，不，他们不知道。我从没告诉过任何人。我说，是啊，但他们知道所有其他在巴尔的摩出生的人的社会安全号码。你的就是剩下的那一个。你也知道，这是真的，对吧？我们推断出的数据，就是已知数据之间空隙里的数据——前提是我们知道得足够多。

cues.en: So where we live has become a place in which it would be very unwise to say about anything that it isn't known if you are pretty widely known in the net. And all of us, for one reason or another, are pretty widely known in the net. We want to live there. It is our neighborhood. We just don't want to live with a video camera on every tree and a microphone on every bush and a data miner beneath our feet everywhere we walk. And the net's like that now.
cues.zh: 所以，我们生活的地方已经变成这样：如果你在网上颇有名气，那还说任何东西不为人知，就非常不明智了。而我们所有人，出于这样那样的原因，在网上都颇有名气。我们想住在那里。那是我们的街区。我们只是不想住在一个每棵树上都有摄像头、每丛灌木里都有麦克风、走到哪儿脚下都有数据挖掘者的地方。而现在的网络就是这样。

cues.en: I'm not objecting to the presence of AOL newbies in Usenet news. It's not an aesthetic judgment from 1995. The neighborhood is now full of people who don't share our ethnocentric techno geekery. I'm not lamenting progress of a sort of democratizing kind.
cues.zh: 我并不是反对 AOL 新手出现在 Usenet 新闻组里。这不是 1995 年那种审美判断。如今这个圈子里满是不认同我们那套以自我为中心的技术极客趣味的人。我并不是在哀叹那种民主化意义上的进步。

cues.en: On the contrary, I'm lamenting progress of a totalizing kind. I'm lamenting progress hostile to human freedom. We all know that it's hostile to human freedom. We all understand its dystopic possibilities because the dystopias of which it is fertile were the stuff of the science fiction that we read when we were children. The Cold War was fertile in the fantastic invention of where we live now and...
cues.zh: 恰恰相反，我哀叹的是那种总体化意义上的进步。我哀叹的是敌视人类自由的进步。我们都知道它敌视人类自由。我们都明白它可能带来的反乌托邦前景，因为它所孕育的那些反乌托邦，正是我们小时候读的科幻小说的题材。冷战孕育了今天我们身处其中的这个世界的种种奇妙发明，而且……

cues.en: It's hard for us to accept that, but it's true. Fortunately, of course, it's not owned by the government. Well, it is. It's fortunate. It's true. It's fortunate that it's owned by people who you can bribe to get the thing no matter who you are. If you're the government, you have easy ways of doing it. You fill out a subpoena bank and you mail it. I spent two hours yesterday with a law school class.
cues.zh: 我们很难接受这一点，但这是真的。幸运的是，它当然不归政府所有。嗯，其实归政府所有。这很幸运。这是真的。幸运的是，它归一些人所有；不管你是谁，你都可以贿赂他们拿到那东西。如果你是政府，你就有简单的办法做到这件事。你填一张传票表格，然后寄出去。昨天我和一个法学院班级待了两个小时。

cues.en: explaining in detail why the Fourth Amendment doesn't exist anymore. And I'm not going to do it again because that's Thursday night and we would do that on a Friday night. But the Fourth Amendment doesn't exist anymore. I'll put the audio on then at the FBI and you can listen to it anytime you want. We have to fess up. If we're the people who care about freedom, it's late in the game and we're behind.
cues.zh: 详细解释为什么第四修正案已经不复存在了。我不打算再讲一遍，因为那是周四晚上的内容，而我们会在周五晚上讲那个。但第四修正案已经不复存在了。到时候我会把音频放到 FBI 那儿，你随时都可以听。我们得承认。如果我们就是那些关心自由的人，那现在已经是后期了，我们落后了。

cues.en: We did a lot of good stuff and we have a lot of tools lying around that we built over the last 25 years. I helped people build those tools. I helped people keep those tools safe. I helped people prevent the monopoly from putting all those tools in its bag and walking off with them. And I'm glad the tools are around, but we do have to admit we have not used them to protect freedom because freedom is decaying. And that's what David meant in his very kind introduction.
cues.zh: 我们做了很多好事，过去 25 年里也积累了很多工具。我帮人们打造这些工具。我帮人们保护好这些工具。我帮人们阻止垄断者把所有这些工具装进自己的袋子一走了之。我很高兴这些工具还在，但我们必须承认，我们并没有用它们来保护自由，因为自由正在衰退。这就是 David 在他那番非常友善的介绍里想表达的意思。

cues.en: In fact, people who are investing in the new enterprises of unfreedom are also the people you will hear if you hang out in Silicon Valley these days telling you that open source has become irrelevant. What's their logic? Their logic is software as a service is becoming the way of the world. Since nobody ever gets any software anymore,
cues.zh: 事实上，那些投资于新的不自由企业的人，也正是你最近混迹硅谷时会听到的人，他们会告诉你开源已经变得无关紧要。他们的逻辑是什么？他们的逻辑是，软件即服务正在成为世界潮流。既然没人再真正拿到软件了，

cues.en: The licenses that say if you give people software, you have to give them freedom don't matter because you're not giving anybody software. You're only giving them services. Well, that's right. Open source doesn't matter. Free software matters a lot. Because of course, free software is open source software with freedom. As Solomon was right, it's the freedom that matters. The rest of it is just source code. Freedom still matters.
cues.zh: 那些规定“如果你把软件给人们，就必须给他们自由”的许可证就不重要了，因为你并没有把软件给任何人。你只是给他们服务。嗯，没错。开源无关紧要。自由软件却非常重要。因为当然，自由软件是带有自由的开源软件。正如 Solomon 说得对，重要的是自由。其余部分只是源代码。自由仍然重要。

cues.en: And what we need to do is to make free software matter to the problem that we have, which is unfree services delivered in unfree ways really beginning to deteriorate the structure of human freedom. Like a lot of unfreedom, the real underlying social process that forces this unfreedom along is nothing more than perceived convenience. All sorts of freedom goes over perceived convenience.
cues.zh: 我们要做的，是让自由软件真正作用于我们面临的问题——以非自由的方式提供的非自由服务，正在开始侵蚀人类自由的结构。和许多不自由一样，真正推动这种不自由的深层社会过程，不过是“感知中的便利”。各种各样的自由，都让位给了感知中的便利。

cues.en: You know this, you stop paying for things with cash. You use a card, you can wave at a RFID reader. Convenience is said to dictate that you need free web hosting and PHP doodads in return for spying all the time because web servers are so terrible to run. Who could run a web server of his own and keep the logs? It would be brutal.
cues.zh: 你知道的，你不再用现金付钱。你用卡，对着 RFID 读卡器挥一下就行。人们说便利决定了一切：你需要免费的网站托管和 PHP 小玩意儿，代价是时时刻刻被监视，因为网站服务器实在太难跑了。谁能自己跑一台网站服务器，还保留日志呢？那简直是受罪。

cues.en: Well, it wouldn't be where I asked, right? It was intended to be a self-fulfilling. Yeah, it was designed to say, you're a client. I'm a server. I invented Windows 7. It was my idea. I'll keep the logs. Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 嗯，它不会在我要求的位置，对吧？它本来就是要自我实现的。对，它设计出来就是说：你是客户端，我是服务器。Windows 7 是我发明的。这是我的主意。日志我来保存。非常感谢。

cues.en: That was the industry. We built another industry. It's in here. But it's not in, well, yeah, it's sort of, yeah, it is kind of in here, huh? So where isn't it? Well, it's not in the personal web server I don't have that would prevent me from falling. Well, why don't we do something about that? So what do we need? We need a really good web server you can put in your pocket and plug in any place.
cues.zh: 那就是这个行业。我们又建了另一个行业。它就在这里。但它不在，嗯，对，它算是，对，它确实算在这里，是吧？那它不在哪儿？嗯，它不在我没有的那个个人 Web 服务器里，那个本可以防止我掉下去。嗯，那我们为什么不想办法解决呢？所以我们需要什么？我们需要一个真正好用的 Web 服务器，能放进口袋，插到任何地方。

cues.en: In other words, it shouldn't be any larger than the charger for your cell phone. And you should be able to plug it in to any power jack in the world and any wire near it or to sync it up to any wifi router that happens to be in this neighborhood. You should have a couple of USB ports that attach it to things. It should know how to bring itself up. It should know how to start its web server.
cues.zh: 换句话说，它不应该比你的手机充电器更大。而且它应该能插上世界上任何一个电源插座，连接附近的任何一根网线，或者同步到附近任何一个碰巧存在的 WiFi 路由器。它应该有几个 USB 接口，用来连接其他设备。它应该知道如何把自己启动起来。它应该知道如何启动自己的 Web 服务器。

cues.en: It should know how to go and collect your stuff out of all the social networking places where you've got it. It should know how to send an encrypted backup of everything to your friend's servers. It should know how to microblog. It should know how to make some noise that's like tweet, but not going to infringe anybody's trademark.
cues.zh: 它应该知道如何从你存放内容的所有社交网络站点上把你的东西收集回来。它应该知道如何把所有内容的加密备份发送到你朋友的服务器上。它应该知道如何发微博。它应该知道如何发出某种类似 tweet 的声音，但又不会侵犯任何人的商标。

cues.en: In other words, you should know how to be your... Oh, excuse me, I've got to use a dangerous word, avatar, in a free net that works for you and keeps the logs. You can always tell what's happening in your server, and if anybody else wants to know what's happening in your server, they can get a search warrant. And if you feel like moving your server,
cues.zh: 换句话说，你应该知道怎么成为你的……哦，抱歉，我得用个危险词，avatar，在一个为你服务、保留日志的自由网络里。你总能知道你的服务器上发生了什么；如果别人想知道你的服务器上发生了什么，他们得拿到搜查令。而如果你想把服务器搬到

cues.en: to Oceana or Sealand or New Zealand or the North Pole. Well, buy a plane ticket and put it in your pocket. Take it there. Leave it behind. Now there's a little more we gotta do, but you know, it's all trivial. We need some dynamic DNS and it's all stuff we've already invented. It's all there. Nobody needs anything special. Do we have the server you can put in your pocket? Indeed we do. Off-the-shelf hardware now, right?
cues.zh: Oceana、Sealand、新西兰或北极。那就买张机票，把它揣进口袋，带到那儿，留在那儿。现在我们还得再做一点事，但你知道，都是小事。我们需要动态 DNS，都是我们已经发明好的东西，全都在那儿，不需要什么特殊的东西。我们有能放进口袋的服务器吗？当然有。现在都是现成硬件，对吧？

cues.en: Beautiful little wall warts made with arm chips. Exactly what I expect for you. Plug them in, plug them in, wire them up. How's the software stack in there? I don't know, gee, it's any software stack you want to put in there. Open to 904, 910, 804, 810, Debian, Red, Fedora, the matter, you can do it in an instant. In fact, I'll send it to you with somebody's top of the charts current.
cues.zh: 漂亮的小型 ARM 芯片墙插电源。正是我为你准备的。插上，插上，接好线。里面的软件栈怎么样？我不知道，天哪，你想往里装什么软件栈都行。Ubuntu 9.04、9.10、8.04、8.10，Debian、Red Hat、Fedora，也一样，瞬间就能搞定。事实上，我会把它连同一个排行榜榜首的当前版本一起发给你。

cues.en: distro in it, you just have to name which one you want. Which one do you want? Well, you ought to want the Debbie and GNU Linux social networking stack. Delivered to you free. Free as in freedom, I mean. Which does all the things I name. Brace itself up, runs its little Apache or its whole IO author, its tiny light, HTTP lighting, whatever you want.
cues.zh: 里面装的发行版，你只要说出想要哪个。你想要哪个？嗯，你应该会想要 Debian GNU/Linux 社交网络栈。免费送到你手上。我是说，自由意义上的免费。它能做我点名的所有事。自己启动起来，跑着它的小 Apache，或者自己的 I/O 服务、小巧的 lighttpd HTTP 服务器，随你想要。

cues.en: Does all the things we needed to do, syncs up, gets your social network data from the places, locks it down, does all your backup searches, finds your friends, registers your dynamic DNS. All this trivial. We know all this is stuff we've got. We need to put that together. I'm not talking about a thing that's hard for us. We need to make a free software distribution device. How many of those do we do? Right?
cues.zh: 它完成我们需要的所有事情，同步，从各处获取你的社交网络数据，把它锁好，做完你的所有备份搜索，找到你的朋友，注册你的动态 DNS。这些都微不足道。我们知道这些我们都已经有了。我们需要把它们整合起来。我不是在说一件对我们来说很难的事。我们需要做一个自由软件分发设备。这种事我们做过多少？对吧？

cues.en: We need to give a bunch to all our friends, and we need to say here, fool around with this and make it better. We need to do the one thing we are really, really, really, really good at. Because all the rest of it is done, in the bag, cheap ready. Those Walmart servers, those are 99 now going to 79. When they're 5 million of them, they'll be 29.99. Then we go to people and we say, 29.99 once, for a lifetime.
cues.zh: 我们需要给所有朋友一大堆，还要在这里说：随便折腾这个，把它做得更好。我们需要做那件我们真正、真正、真正、真正擅长的事。因为其余的都完成了，稳了，便宜又现成。那些 Walmart 服务器，现在 99，要降到 79。等它们有 500 万台时，就会降到 29.99。然后我们去找人们说：29.99，一次付费，终身使用。

cues.en: Great social networking, updates, automatically. Software so strong you couldn't knock it over if you kicked it. Used in hundreds of millions of servers all over the planet doing a wonderful job. And you know what? You get no spying for free. Right? They want to know what's going on and they'll let them get a search warrant.
cues.zh: 很棒的社交网络，自动更新。软件强到你踹都踹不倒。全球数亿台服务器都在用，干得漂亮。而且你知道吗？想监视？没免费的。对吧？他们想知道发生了什么，就得先拿到搜查令。

cues.en: For your apartment, your home, your castle, the place where the Fourth Amendment still sort of exists every other Tuesday and Thursday when the Supreme Court's not in session. We can do that. We can do that. That requires us to do only the stuff we're really, really good at. The rest of it, we get for free. Mr. Zuckerberg, not so much.
cues.zh: 为你的公寓、你的家、你的城堡——那个第四修正案还勉强有效的地方，在最高法院休庭时，隔周的周二和周四还算数。我们能做。我们能做。这要求我们只做自己真正、真正擅长的事。其余的就白拿。扎克伯格先生，就没这待遇了。

cues.en: Because, of course, when there is a competitor to all spying all the time, whether you like it or not, the competition is going to do real well. Don't expect Google to be the competitor. That's our platform. What we need is to make a thing that's so greasy that there will never be another social network platform again. Right? Can we do it? Yeah. Absolutely.
cues.zh: 因为，当然，当一个对手全天候监视一切时，不管你喜欢与否，这个竞争者都会做得非常成功。别指望 Google 来当这个竞争者。那是我们的平台。我们需要做的，是做出一个黏性极强的东西，让以后再也不会有另一个社交网络平台。对吧？我们能做到吗？能。绝对能。

cues.en: In fact, if you don't have a date on Friday night, let's just have a hack fest and get it done. Right? It's well within our reach. We're going to do it before the Facebook IPO. We're going to wait until after. Really? Honestly? Seriously? See, the problem that the law has very often in the world where we live and practice and work, the problem that the law has is very often the problem that technology can solve.
cues.zh: 事实上，如果你周五晚上没约会，那我们就来场编程狂欢把它搞定。对吧？这完全在我们能力范围内。我们要在 Facebook IPO 之前做成。我们要等到之后再说。真的吗？说实话？认真的？看吧，在我们生活、实践和工作的这个世界里，法律经常遇到的问题，往往正是技术能解决的问题。

cues.en: And the problem that technology can solve is the place where we go to the law. That's the free software movement, right? There's software hacking over here, and there's legal hacking over there, and you put them both together, and the hole is bigger than some of the parts. So it's not like we have to live in the catastrophe. We don't have to live in the catastrophe. It's not like what we have to do to begin to reverse the catastrophe is hard for us.
cues.zh: 技术能解决的问题，正是我们求诸法律的地方。那就是自由软件运动，对吧？这边是软件黑客，那边是法律黑客，把两者放在一起，这个缺口比某些部分还大。所以并不是说我们非得生活在灾难之中。我们不必生活在灾难之中。要开始扭转这场灾难，我们该做的事并不算难。

cues.en: We need to re-architect services in the net. We need to redistribute services back towards the edge. We need to de-virtualize the servers where your life is stored. And we need to restore some autonomy to you as the owner of the server. The measures for taking those steps are technical. As usual,
cues.zh: 我们需要重新架构网络中的服务。我们需要把服务重新分布回边缘。我们需要把你生活数据所在的服务器去虚拟化。我们还需要让你作为服务器所有者恢复一部分自主权。采取这些步骤靠的是技术手段。像往常一样，

cues.en: the box builders are ahead of us. The hardware isn't the constraint. As usual, nowadays, the software isn't really that deep a constraint either because we've made so much wonderful software, which is in fact being used by all the guys on the bad architecture. They don't want to do without our stuff. The bad architecture is enabled powered by us. The re-architecture is too.
cues.zh: 造盒子的人走在我们前面。硬件不是约束。像往常一样，如今软件也不算是那么深层的约束，因为我们做出了这么多出色的软件，而坏架构上的所有人其实都在用这些软件。他们不想少了我们的东西。坏架构是由我们赋能、由我们驱动的。重新架构也是如此。

cues.en: And we have our usual magic benefit. If we had one copy of what I'm talking about, we'd have all the copies we need. We have no manufacturing or transport or logistics constraint. If we do the job, it's done. We scale. This is a technical challenge for a social reason. It's a frontier for technical people to explore. There is enormous social payoff.
cues.zh: 我们还有通常那种神奇优势。如果我说的东西只要有一份，我们就有了所需的全部副本。我们不受制造、运输或物流的限制。只要我们做成这件事，它就完成了。我们就能扩展。这是一项出于社会原因的技术挑战。它是技术人员可以探索的前沿。社会回报巨大。

cues.en: for exploring it. The payoff is plain because the harm being ameliorated is current and people you know are suffering from it. Everything we know about why we make free software says that's when we come into our own. It's a technical challenge, incrementally attainable by extension from where we already are,
cues.zh: 去探索它。回报显而易见，因为正在减轻的伤害就在当下，你认识的人正受其苦。我们做自由软件的全部经验都表明，那正是我们大显身手的时候。这是一项技术挑战，可以从现有基础逐步扩展实现，

cues.en: that makes the lives of the people around us and whom we care about immediately better. I have never, in 25 years of doing this work, I have never seen us fail to rise to a challenge that could be defined in those terms. So I don't think we're going to fail this one either. Mr. Zuckerberg richly deserves bankruptcy. Let's give it to him. Let's give it to him. For free. For free.
cues.zh: 让周围的人和我们关心的人的生活立刻变得更好。做这项工作25年来，我从未见过我们在能用这些标准定义的挑战面前失败。所以我认为这次我们也不会失败。扎克伯格先生完全活该破产。让他破产吧。让他破产吧。免费。免费。

cues.en: I promise, and you should promise to not to spy on the bankruptcy proceed. It's none of our business. It's private. This is actually, you know, a story potentially happy. It is a story potentially happy. And if we do it, then we will have quelled one more rumor about the irrelevance of us. And everybody in the Valley will have to go find another buzzword.
cues.zh: 我保证，你也该保证不去窥探破产程序。那不关我们的事，是私事。其实这可能是个皆大欢喜的故事。这确实可能是个皆大欢喜的故事。如果我们这么做了，就能再平息一个说我们无关紧要的传言。硅谷的每个人就都得去找下一个流行词了。

cues.en: And all the guys who think that Sand Hill Road is going to rise into new power and glory by spying on everybody and monetizing it will have to find another line of work too. All of which is purely on the side of the angels. Purely on the side of the angels. We will not be rid of all our problems by any means. But just moving the logs from them to you is the single biggest step that we can take
cues.zh: 而那些以为 Sand Hill Road 能靠监视所有人并从中牟利、重获权势与荣耀的人，也得另谋出路。这一切完全站在道义一边。完全站在道义一边。我们绝不会因此摆脱所有问题。但仅仅把日志从他们那里挪到你们这里，就是我们能迈出的最大一步。

cues.en: in resolving a whole range of social problems, that I feel badly in what remains of my American constitution, and that I would feel badly about if I were watching the failure of European data protection law from inside instead of outside, and that I would feel kind of hopeful about if I were, oh, say, a friend of mine in China. Because, you know, of course, we really ought to put a VPN in that wallboard, and probably we ought to put a tour router.
cues.zh: 在解决一系列社会问题这件事上，我身上残存的那点美国特质让我感觉糟糕；如果我是在欧洲内部、而不是从外部看着欧洲数据保护法失败，我也会感觉糟糕；如果我是一个——比如说——我在中国的朋友，我甚至会有点抱有希望。因为你知道，当然，我们真该在那块墙板里装个 VPN，可能还该装个 Tor 路由器。

cues.en: And of course we got BitTorrent. And by the time you get done with all of that, we have a freedom box. We have a box that not merely climbs us out of the hole we're in, we have a box that actually puts the ladder up for people who are deeper in the hole than we are. Which is another thing we love to do. I do believe the United States State Department will go slanging away at the Chinese Communist Party for a year or two about internet freedom.
cues.zh: 当然，我们还有 BitTorrent。等把这一切都做完，我们就有了一个 FreedomBox。这个盒子不仅能让我们爬出自己所在的坑，还能为那些陷得比我们更深的人架起梯子。这也是我们喜欢做的另一件事。我确实相信，美国国务院会围绕互联网自由，对中国共产党的猛烈抨击持续一两年。

cues.en: And I believe the Chinese Communist Party are going to go slanging back. And what they're going to say is, you think you've got real good privacy and autonomy in the internet over in your neighborhood? And I've got to admit, every time they do that now, as they have been doing in the last two weeks, I would say ouch if I was Hillary Clinton and I knew anything about it. Because we don't. Because we don't. It's true. We have a capitalist kind, and they've got a centralist.
cues.zh: 我相信中国共产党会反唇相讥。他们会说：你以为你们自己那一带的互联网真有很好的隐私和自主权吗？我得承认，现在每次他们这么说——过去两周他们一直这么说——如果我是希拉里·克林顿，而且对此略知一二，我会说“哎哟”。因为我们没有。因为我们没有。这是真的。我们有的是资本主义那种，他们有中央集权那种。

cues.en: vanguard of the party sort of Marxist kind, or maybe Marxist, maybe just totalitarian kind. But we're not going to win the freedom of the net discussion carrying Facebook on our backs. We're not. But just through those war wars servers around pretty thickly in American society and start taking back the logs, and if you want to know who I talked to on a Friday night, get a search warrant and stop reading my email.
cues.zh: 党的先锋队，某种马克思主义式的，或者也许是马克思主义，或者也许只是极权主义式的。但我们背着 Facebook 是赢不了关于网络自由的讨论的。我们赢不了。但只要把那些 war wars 服务器相当密集地铺进美国社会，并开始收回日志；如果你想知道我周五晚上和谁说过话，就去拿搜查令，别再读我的邮件。

cues.en: And by the way, there's my GPG key in there and now we really are encrypting for a change and so on and so on and so on. And it begins to look like something we really might want to go on an international crusade about. We really are making freedom here for other people too. For people who live in places where the web don't work. So this is not a challenge we don't want to rise to. This is a challenge we want to rise to plenty. In fact...
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我的 GPG 密钥就在里面，现在我们总算真的在加密了，等等等等。这开始看起来像是一件我们真该发起一场国际运动去推动的事了。我们在这里也确实是在为其他人创造自由。为那些生活在网络用不了的地方的人。所以，这不是我们不想迎战的挑战。这是我们非常想迎战的挑战。事实上……

cues.en: We're in a happy state that all the benefits we can get are way bigger than the technical intricacy of doing what needs to be done, which isn't much. Isn't much. That's where we came from. We came from our technology was more free than we understood and we gave away a bunch of the freedom before we really knew it was gone. We came from unfree software had bad social consequences further down the road than even the freedom agitators knew. We came from
cues.zh: 我们现在的处境很幸运：我们能得到的所有好处，都远远大于完成必要工作所需的技术复杂度，而要做的事并不多。并不多。我们就是从那里来的。我们来自这样一个起点：我们的技术比我们以为的更自由，而我们在真正意识到自由已经失去之前，就放弃了一大堆自由。我们来自这样一个起点：非自由软件造成了糟糕的社会后果，其影响之深远，连自由倡导者都不知道。我们来自

cues.en: Unfreedom's metaphors tend to produce bad technology. In other words, we came from stuff that our movement, if I can call it ours, was designed to confront from the beginning. But we came from there. And we're still living with the consequences of we didn't do it quite right the first time. Though we caught up, thanks to Richard Stallman, and we're moving on. Where we live now is no place we're going to have to see our grandchildren.
cues.zh: 非自由的隐喻往往会制造糟糕的技术。换句话说，我们来自那些东西，而我们的运动——如果我能称它为我们的运动——从一开始就是为了对抗这些东西。但我们确实来自那里。而且我们仍在承受第一次没有做对所带来的后果。不过，多亏了 Richard Stallman，我们赶上来了，并且还在继续前进。我们现在所处的境地，绝不是将来要让子孙后代面对的那种境地。

cues.en: where we live now is no place we would like to conduct guided tours of. I used to say to my students, how many video cameras are there between where you live and the law school? Count them. I now say to my students, how many video cameras are there between the front door of the law school and this classroom? Count them. I now say to my students, can you find a place where there are no video cameras? Now, what happened in that process was that we created immense
cues.zh: 我们现在生活的地方，绝不是我们愿意带人参观导览的地方。我以前常对学生说，从你住的地方到法学院，一路上有多少摄像头？数数看。我现在对学生说，从法学院前门到这间教室，有多少摄像头？数数看。我现在又对学生说，你能找到一个没有摄像头的地方吗？在这个过程中发生的是，我们创造了庞大的

cues.en: cognitive auxiliaries for the state. Enormous engines of listening. You know how it is if you live in an American university thanks to the movie and music companies which keep reminding you of the consequences of living in the midst of an enormous surveillance network. We're surrounded by stuff listening to and watching us. We're surrounded by mineable data. Not all...
cues.zh: 为国家服务的认知辅助工具。巨大的监听引擎。如果你在美国大学里生活，就知道那是什么滋味——电影和音乐公司不断提醒你，生活在庞大监控网络之中会有什么后果。我们周围全是监听和监视我们的东西。我们周围全是可挖掘的数据。并非所有……

cues.en: All of that's going to go away because we took Facebook and split it up and carried away our little shards of it. It's not going to go away because we won't take free web hosting with spying inside. We'll have other work to do. And some of that work is lawyer's work. I will admit that. Some of that work is law drafting, litigating, making trouble, and doing lawyer stuff. And that's fine.
cues.zh: 这一切都会消失，因为我们已经把 Facebook 拆开，各自拿走了一小片。它不会因为我们不接受内置监控的免费网页托管就消失。我们还有别的工作要做。其中一些是律师的活儿。我承认。有些工作是起草法律、打官司、制造麻烦，干律师那一套。这没问题。

cues.en: Ready. My friends and I will do the lawyers. It would be way simpler to do the lawyers' work if we were living in a society which had come to understand its privacy better. It would be way simpler to do the lawyers' work if young people realized that when they grow up and start voting, or start voting now that they're grown up, this is an issue. That they need to get the rest of it done the way we fix the big stuff when we were kids.
cues.zh: 准备好了。律师那部分由我和朋友们来做。如果我们生活在一个更懂得理解隐私的社会里，律师这摊活儿会简单得多。如果年轻人意识到，等他们长大开始投票——或者既然已经长大、现在就开始投票——这是一个议题，律师这摊活儿也会简单得多。他们需要像我们小时候解决那些大问题那样，把剩下的也搞定。

cues.en: We'll have a much easier time with the enormous confusions of international interlocking of regimes when we have deteriorated the immense force of American capitalism in forcing us to be less free and more surveilled for other people's profit all the time. It isn't that this gets all the problems solved.
cues.zh: 等我们削弱了美国资本主义的巨大力量——它一直迫使我们为了别人的利润变得更不自由、受到更多监控——处理国际制度相互勾连带来的巨大混乱就会容易得多。这并不意味着所有问题都解决了。

cues.en: But the easy work is very rich and rewarding right now. The problems are really bad. Getting the easy ones out will improve the politics for solving the hard ones. And it's right up our alley. The solution is made of our parts. We got to do it. That's my message. It's Friday night. Some people don't want to go right back to coding, I'm sure.
cues.zh: 但眼下简单的工作回报丰厚，也很有成就感。问题确实很严重。先把容易的解决掉，会改善解决难题的政治环境。而这正是我们的拿手好戏。解决方案就是由我们这些部分拼成的。我们必须去做。这就是我要传达的。现在是周五晚上。我敢肯定，有些人不想马上回去写代码。

cues.en: We could put it off until Tuesday. But how long do you really want to wait? How long do you really want to wait? You know every day that goes by there's more data we'll never get back. Every day that goes by there's more inferences we can't undo. Every day that goes by we pile up more stuff in the hands of the people who got too much. So it's not like we should just sort of say one of these days I'll get around to that. It's not like we should say, you know,
cues.zh: 我们本可以把它拖到周二。但你真的想等多久？你真的想等多久？你知道，每过去一天，就有更多数据我们再也拿不回来。每过去一天，就有更多推断我们无法撤销。每过去一天，我们就把更多东西堆到那些已经拥有太多的人手里。所以不是随便说一句“改天我有空再处理”就行。也不是说，你知道，

cues.en: I think I'd rather sort of spend my time browsing news about iPad. It's way more urgent than that. It's way more urgent than that. It's that we haven't given ourselves the direction in which to go. So let's give ourselves the direction in which to go. The direction in which to go is towards freedom using free software to make social justice.
cues.zh: 我觉得我宁愿花时间刷 iPad 新闻。这比那紧急得多。这比那紧急得多。问题在于，我们还没给自己定下前进方向。那就给自己定下前进方向。前进方向就是走向自由，用自由软件实现社会正义。

cues.en: But you know this, okay? That's the problem with talking on a Friday night. You talk for an hour and all you tell people is what they know already. So thanks a lot. I'm happy to take your questions.
cues.zh: 但你们知道这个，对吧？周五晚上演讲的问题就在这儿。你讲了一个小时，结果告诉大家的都是他们早就知道的东西。所以非常感谢。我很乐意回答你们的问题。
